udt_union_v0.doc:
The document caps a compiler enforces, as [`PerchDocCompiler::limits`]
returns them. Versioned: a later budget (a complexity-weighted one, say)
is a new variant, which a consumer that does not know it refuses rather
than misreads.
udt_union_v0.name: DocLimits

udt_union_v0.doc: Where a compiled rule applies. `SelfAdmin` is account-agnostic: the\napplying account resolves it to its own address.
udt_union_v0.name: RuleScope

void_v0.doc: Calls to the applying account itself (`CallContract(self)`).
void_v0.name: SelfAdmin

tuple_v0.doc: Calls to this contract.
tuple_v0.name: Contract

udt_struct_v0.doc: A cumulative spend cap lowered to OZ `spending_limit`'s install params\n(`SpendingLimitAccountParams`). The tracked token is the rule's scope\ncontract, so it is not carried here.
udt_struct_v0.name: CompiledCap

fields.doc: Rolling-window length in ledgers.
fields.name: period_ledgers

fields.doc: Cumulative amount ceiling over the rolling window.
fields.name: spending_limit

udt_struct_v0.doc: A compiled document: its canonical identity and the rules it becomes.
udt_struct_v0.name: CompiledDoc

fields.doc: The canonical bytes `doc_hash` is the hash of. The account stores\nthem so anyone, including the recovery controller, can read back the\nfull applied document.
fields.name: canonical

fields.doc: `sha256(canonical bytes)` \xe2\x80\x94 the hash the reviewer approved. Formatting\nof the submitted JSON is irrelevant: a pretty-printed file and its\nminified twin compile to the same hash.
fields.name: doc_hash

fields.doc:
The fingerprint (`perch_recovery_interface::credential::Credential::
fingerprint`) of every declared signer's credential, with external
keys canonicalized by their verifier. What revocation compares
(spec \xc2\xa78).
fields.name: fingerprints

fields.doc:
The compiled `recovery` member: zero or one entries (a `Vec` for the
same reason as [`CompiledRule::install`]). Present \xe2\x87\x92 the document
enrolls account recovery, and the applier syncs this configuration to
the controller instance it names (`docs/recovery/`).
fields.name: recovery

fields.doc: One compiled rule per document rule, in the submitted order.
fields.name: rules

udt_struct_v0.doc: One rule, compiled to the exact shapes OZ's `add_context_rule` takes:\nresolved addresses, OZ `Signer`s, and (for constrained rules) the\ninterpreter program as `InstallParams`.
udt_struct_v0.name: CompiledRule

fields.doc:
Zero or one entries (a `Vec` for the same reason as `install`).
Present \xe2\x87\x92 also attach OZ `spending_limit` with these params \xe2\x80\x94 the
cumulative cap the stateless interpreter cannot express. The applier
resolves the policy's content-addressed address and keys it into the
rule's policy map beside the interpreter; the tracked token is the
rule's `Contract` scope (validation pins `token == scope`).
fields.name: cap

fields.doc:
The interpreter program to attach: zero or one entries. A `Vec`
because `#[contracttype]` has no conversion for `Option` of a custom
struct (`Option<u32>` on `valid_until` works because `u32` is a host
type). Empty \xe2\x87\x92 a policy-free rule.
fields.name: install

fields.doc: The rule's name in the document. The account matches installed rules\nby name and scope.
fields.name: name

fields.doc: The rule's signers, with external keys as declared (already\nverifier-canonical).
fields.name: signers

fields.doc: The last ledger the rule authorizes, if bounded: OZ's inclusive\n`valid_until`, one below the document's `not-after-ledger`.
fields.name: valid_until

udt_struct_v0.doc: What `derive_target` returns: the recovery target the controller binds\ninto an attempt's statement (spec \xc2\xa77.1).
udt_struct_v0.name: DerivedTarget

fields.doc: The target's canonical bytes: exactly what the completing `apply_doc`\nmust submit.
fields.name: canonical

fields.doc: The target's recovery `config_hash` (the current one, or the current\none with the declared ZK rotation).
fields.name: config_hash

fields.doc: `sha256` of `canonical`: the target's `doc_hash`.
fields.name: doc_hash

fields.doc: Fingerprints of every credential in the target (spec \xc2\xa77.3 rule 7).
fields.name: fingerprints

fields.doc:
The credentials occupying the replaced signer slots in the source:
the applied document's for lost-key, the baseline's for compromise.
External keys are canonicalized by their verifier, so a credential's
`fingerprint` is the one revocation compares. The controller records
them at T1 and the completion revokes them (spec \xc2\xa78).
fields.name: replaced

udt_error_enum_v0.doc: Everything `compile_doc` can refuse. (`#[scerr]` assigns sequential codes\nfrom 1, in variant order.)
udt_error_enum_v0.name: DocCompilerError

cases.doc: The submitted document bytes are not UTF-8.
cases.name: DocNotUtf8

cases.doc: The document failed fail-closed parsing (unknown field, bad shape, unsupported version, duplicate key, \xe2\x80\xa6).
cases.name: DocParse

cases.doc: The document failed semantic validation (dangling signer ref, malformed address or key, ambiguous empty list, \xe2\x80\xa6).
cases.name: DocInvalid

cases.doc: The document names no network, or a network that is not this chain.
cases.name: WrongNetwork

cases.doc: The document cannot be lowered to rules (unsupported rule shape).
cases.name: DocCompile

cases.doc: The document exceeds a document cap ([`MAX_DOC_SIGNERS`], [`MAX_DOC_RULES`], [`MAX_DOC_CANONICAL_BYTES`], [`MAX_RULE_NAME_BYTES`]).
cases.name: DocTooLarge

cases.doc: A signer's external `key` is not its verifier-canonical form: either the verifier could not canonicalize it at all, or the declared bytes differ from the canonical form the verifier returns (e.g. a WebAuthn key carrying a credential-id suffix the verifier drops, or a non-canonical point encoding). The compiler refuses it rather than silently canonicalizing, so the bytes the document hash \xe2\x80\x94 and a recovery attempt's `replacements_hash` \xe2\x80\x94 bind are exactly the bytes the installed credential uses, and two signers cannot hide one physical key under two spellings.
cases.name: KeyNotCanonicalizable

cases.doc: `derive_target`: the current document enrolls no recovery.
cases.name: NotEnrolled

cases.doc: `derive_target`: the replacement set breaks spec \xc2\xa77.3 rules 1-3 (not canonical, empty for lost-key, a signer id that is not replaceable or not declared in the source, or a change of credential kind or verifier), or the action is not a recovery attempt.
cases.name: ReplacementRefused

cases.doc: `derive_target`: the ZK enrollment is missing for a ZK mode, present for a guardian-only mode, or reuses the enrolled id.
cases.name: ZkEnrollmentMismatch

cases.doc: `derive_target`: the target has no policy-free self-admin rule with a signer (the anti-brick check).
cases.name: AdminLockout

udt_struct_v0.doc: The canonical form and fragment hashes a compiler produces, as\n[`PerchDocCompiler::capabilities`] returns them.
udt_struct_v0.name: CompilerCapabilities

fields.doc: The CANON version `doc_hash` is `sha256` of (`CANONICAL.md`).
fields.name: canon_version

fields.doc: The domain tag of a recovery member's `config_hash` (spec \xc2\xa73.2).
fields.name: config_hash_tag

fields.doc: The domain tag of a rule's `rule_hash` (spec \xc2\xa73.2).
fields.name: rule_hash_tag

function_v0.doc: The document caps every `compile_doc` and `derive_target` enforces.
function_v0.name: limits

function_v0.doc:
JSON bytes in \xe2\x86\x92 compiled rules + canonical `doc_hash` out. Pure:
no auth, no storage. The document must name THIS network (its
`network` string must hash to the chain's network id), so a testnet
document can never compile on mainnet or vice versa. It must also fit
the document caps ([`Self::limits`]), and every external signer key
must already be its verifier-canonical form: the compiler calls each
named verifier's `batch_canonicalize_key` to check.
function_v0.name: compile_doc

function_v0.doc: The CANON version and the fragment hash domain tags this compiler\nproduces.
function_v0.name: capabilities

function_v0.doc:
Derive a recovery target (`docs/recovery/spec.md` \xc2\xa77): `source_json`
is the account's applied document (lost-key) or the published
baseline (compromise); `current_json` is the applied document, whose
recovery member the target keeps. The target is the source with
exactly the declared replacements and ZK rotation, then validated,
network-bound, capped, compiled, and anti-brick-checked like any
applied document. Pure: no auth, no storage. The controller calls it
when an attempt begins, and completers simulate it to obtain the
canonical bytes.
function_v0.name: derive_target

udt_struct_v0.doc:
What the compiler stores in the interpreter for one `(account, rule)`: the
program plus the provenance hash of the rule it was compiled from. Sharing
this `#[contracttype]` between the compiler and the interpreter is what
keeps install params from ever being a hand-built `ScVal` \xe2\x80\x94 both sides
encode and decode through exactly these types.
udt_struct_v0.name: InstallParams

fields.doc: The source rule's `perch_ir::rule_hash`, not the whole document's\nhash (the field keeps its original name). It binds the on-chain\nprogram to the reviewed rule (provenance for lift/diff).
fields.name: doc_hash

udt_union_v0.doc: A signer credential, shaped like OZ `stellar_accounts::smart_account::Signer`.
udt_union_v0.name: Credential

tuple_v0.doc: `Signer::Delegated(address)`: a `G...` or `C...` address that\nauthenticates through CAP-0071 delegated auth.
tuple_v0.name: Delegated

tuple_v0.doc: `Signer::External(verifier, key)`: a key checked by a verifier\ncontract.
tuple_v0.name: External

udt_struct_v0.doc: One designated signer slot and the credential that replaces whatever\nthat slot holds in the source document.
udt_struct_v0.name: Replacement

fields.doc: The credential the target document gives that signer id.
fields.name: credential

fields.doc: A document signer id listed in the enrolled `recovery.replaceable`.
fields.name: signer_id

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A ZK enrollment a recovery completion installs.

The commitment is bound here, not only the id: completion runs under the
zero-signer recovery rule, so nothing signs its arguments, and a
commitment supplied only at completion could be swapped by whoever
submits the completing transaction first \xe2\x80\x94 handing them the account's
next ZK factor.
udt_struct_v0.name: ZkEnrollment

fields.doc:
The new leaf's inner commitment, `Poseidon2(DOM_LEAF, secret)`.
Derivation writes `id` and `commitment` into the target document's
recovery section, so the target hash binds them, and the completing
`apply_doc` inserts the leaf from the compiled target, never from a
call argument.
fields.name: commitment

fields.doc: The new enrollment id. Must never have been enrolled for this\naccount before.
fields.name: id

udt_struct_v0.doc: Everything a `LostKey`/`Compromise` attempt changes about the source\ndocument. See `docs/recovery/spec.md` \xc2\xa77.
udt_struct_v0.name: ReplacementSet

fields.doc: Signer replacements in strictly ascending `signer_id` byte order\n(sorted, no duplicates) \xe2\x80\x94 the one canonical order.
fields.name: signers

fields.doc:
The fresh ZK enrollment the completion installs, required exactly
when the enrolled mode has a ZK factor (a ZK-evidenced completion
consumes the enrolled credential, so it must install a fresh one).
Empty or one entry \xe2\x80\x94 a `Vec` because `#[contracttype]` cannot derive
`Option<CustomStruct>`.
fields.name: zk_enrollment

udt_enum_v0.doc:
The action domain a statement authorizes. Evidence for one action never
satisfies another: the action code is the encoding's 26th byte and selects
the subject layout, so two statements that differ only in action have
different digests (and different encoded lengths for most pairs).

The numeric codes are part of the wire format.
udt_enum_v0.name: RecoveryAction

cases.doc: Lost-key recovery: replace designated credentials in an agreed\nsnapshot of the current document.
cases.name: LostKey

cases.doc: Compromise recovery: restore the enrolled baseline, with designated\ncredentials replaced.
cases.name: Compromise

cases.doc: Change or remove the enrolled recovery configuration (the evidence a\n`Protected` account needs in addition to owner authorization).
cases.name: Reconfigure

cases.doc: Approve one scheduled account upgrade (the evidence a `Protected`\naccount needs in addition to owner authorization).
cases.name: Upgrade
